solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One seduced by a most bizarre philosophy

indicators.note: being seduced by something means being taken in by it, so one goes inside the other piece
something bizarre is weirdly arranged, so the letters of a most are scrambled

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone lured in by an outlandish creed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bizarre' rearranges A MOST into TAOSM; 'seduced by' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Taoism is the Chinese school of thought founded on the teachings of Laozi.

clue.text: American right-wingers do without alcohol

definitions.meaning: a do is a party, and one serving tea rather than drink is a ...

explanation.surface: US conservatives abstaining from drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tea Party movement is a US right-wing faction; a tea party is a teetotal social gathering.

clue.text: Supervisor pinching typist's bottom, a dangerous manoeuvre

indicators.note: pinching means gripping between, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: an overseer is a supervisor

indicators.note: the bottom of a down word is its last letter

explanation.surface: An office boss behaving badly, a risky move in every sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom' gives T, the last letter of 'typist's'; 'pinching' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Oversteer is a car turning more sharply than the driver intends, a hazardous handling fault.

clue.text: An item on the fast food menu? Definitely not

definitions.text: An item on the fast food menu? Definitely not

parts.words: An item on the fast food menu? Definitely not
parts.note: the dish is food, but nothing about it is fast

explanation.surface: A burger-bar dish, the clue says, then denies it.
explanation.walkthrough: Escargots are eaten as food, but these creatures are proverbially slow, so they are anything but fast food.
explanation.definitionFit: Snails are served as a delicacy yet are a byword for slowness.

clue.text: Rogue captain set adrift with half- sister

parts.note: Captain William Bligh of the Bounty was cast adrift by mutineers

indicators.note: half of the word sister is taken, here its second three letters

explanation.surface: A story of a scoundrel skipper cast off in a boat alongside a sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bounty's captain was famously cast adrift by mutineers; 'half-' takes the back half of the sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: Blighter is British slang for a contemptible or mischievous person, a rascal.

clue.text: Someone like Johnson, a man of many words

definitions.meaning: Samuel Johnson compiled the famous 1755 Dictionary of the English Language
a dictionary maker deals in a vast number of words

explanation.surface: A politician named Johnson is described as talkative.
explanation.walkthrough: Johnson is not the prime minister but Dr Samuel Johnson, the dictionary compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: A lexicographer writes dictionaries, as Samuel Johnson famously did.

clue.text: Change course of fight in Indian province

parts.note: Goa is a state on India's west coast
a bout is a fight, as in boxing

explanation.surface: A sudden shift of direction in a scrap somewhere in India.
explanation.definitionFit: To go about is the sailing term for tacking, turning a vessel onto a new heading.

clue.text: Finalise advice about Brussels

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice
Brussels is the seat of the EU, so stands for it

explanation.surface: Wrap up a recommendation regarding the Belgian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but signals one piece going round the other; Brussels stands for the European Union based there.
explanation.definitionFit: To tie up a deal is to settle or conclude it.

clue.text: Haunt troops during siesta

indicators.note: during means within a period, so this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a siesta is a rest
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Ghosts plaguing soldiers during their afternoon nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' signals a container; OR (other ranks) is the crossword convention for ordinary soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A haunt is a place one frequents, as is a resort in the sense of a favourite spot.

clue.text: One needs an age to go round battlefield

indicators.note: going round means turning back the other way, so the pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: an age is an era

explanation.surface: Someone needs a long time to travel around a battleground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go round' turns ANERA back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a scene of conflict or contest, figuratively a field of battle.

clue.text: Organise a sex party for contributors to Treasury

indicators.note: to organise is to arrange, so the letters of a sex party are set in a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to set up a raunchy gathering, to the benefit of the Exchequer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organise' rearranges A SEX PARTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxpayers fund the national Treasury through the levies they hand over.

clue.text: English colliery that's gone bust on paper

indicators.note: gone bust means broken, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: that's is read as that has, the has linking to the indicator

explanation.surface: A British coal mine that has collapsed into bankruptcy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone bust' rearranges E, COLLIERY and THAT; the 's of that's is 'has', joining the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true on paper holds in principle but not necessarily in practice.

clue.text: Forgive a bishop found with crack

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop
to crack a problem is to solve it

explanation.surface: Pardoning a cleric who has been caught with drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' looks like the drug but is the verb meaning work out.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve someone is to pardon or free them from guilt.

clue.text: Policeman impounding husband's mode of transport

indicators.note: impounding means shutting something in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: copper is slang for a policeman
H is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: An officer seizing a married man's car or bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impounding' puts H inside COPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopper is slang for a helicopter, an aircraft used to travel.

clue.text: Row is a sad sight for the Speaker

indicators.note: what the speaker says is heard, not seen, so a word with the same sound is entered

parts.note: a tear is a sad thing to see

explanation.surface: A quarrel is something the Commons chair finds upsetting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Speaker' suggests the Commons chair, but it signals a word with the same sound as TEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one of a series of rows placed one above another, as in a stadium.

clue.text: Tory left infiltrating Times in clever fashion

indicators.note: infiltrating means getting inside, so these pieces go into the other

parts.note: times as in multiplication, read as by (three by four)
the Tories are the political right

explanation.surface: A Conservative turned left-winger has crept into a national newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' is not the newspaper but multiplication, as in three by four; 'infiltrating' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Brightly can mean smartly or intelligently, as a bright pupil is a clever one.

clue.text: Starry-eyed Romeo leaving tipsily not long ago

indicators.note: tipsily means unsteadily, so the remaining letters are jumbled
leaving means going away, so this letter is dropped

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A dreamy lover staggering off drunk in the recent past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes one R out of STARRYEYED; 'tipsily' rearranges STARYEYED.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesterday can mean the recent past in general as well as the previous day.

clue.text: Wife with husband abandoning her twice for vagabond

parts.note: and means with

indicators.note: twice means the result is written two times
abandoning means leaving, so the letter goes from the word

explanation.surface: A spouse whose man deserts her twice over for a drifter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' drops H from HER leaving ER, and 'twice' doubles it to ERER.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanderer roams from place to place, like a vagabond.

clue.text: Victim in genuine denial

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

parts.note: genuine means real
the butt of a joke is its victim

explanation.surface: A wronged party making a sincere refusal of the charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container; the victim is the butt of a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuttal is a contradiction or refutation of a claim.

clue.text: Al fresco occasions for vacuous young women?

definitions.meaning: Australian and British slang for barbecues, held outdoors
a Barbie, after the doll, is an attractive but empty-headed young woman

explanation.surface: Outdoor parties attended by shallow young women.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbies are barbecues, outdoor meals; the doll's name is used mockingly for vapid young women.

clue.text: Some samosas I ate, originating here?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A diner muses that the samosas eaten came from this part of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Samosas are a South Asian snack, so this continent is where they come from.

clue.text: Sailor runs up to welcome Bill

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so one piece holds the other
in a down clue up means read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: goes means runs
an ad is a bill, a poster or notice

explanation.surface: A seaman hurries upstairs to greet someone called Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the word for runs upward in this down clue, giving SEOG; 'to welcome' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea dog is an old or experienced sailor.

clue.text: Engineer keeling over in old American capital

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second
keeling over means toppling, so the word is turned backwards

parts.note: James Watt was the Scottish engineer of steam engine fame

explanation.surface: A mechanic collapsing in an old US city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeling over' gives TTAW, the engineer's name backwards; 'in' signals the container. 'American capital' wants to be the definition; only 'capital' is.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada.

clue.text: Intestinal trouble in Crete

indicators.note: trouble suggests disorder, so the letters of in Crete are jumbled

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker's stomach upset on a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges IN CRETE.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteric describes things of the gut, from the Greek enteron, bowel.

clue.text: Vehicle manufactured by a large firm from the south

indicators.note: in a down clue, from the south means read from the bottom up, so reversed

parts.note: set means firm, as jelly sets

explanation.surface: A car built by a big company in the southern hemisphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a company but means solid. 'from the south' reverses ALSET.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tesla is an electric car made by the company of that name.

clue.text: H for an impetuous chap?

parts.note: read the answer as an instruction: the head (first letter) of hot is the single letter in the clue

explanation.surface: A single letter offered as shorthand for a rash fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: split the answer as HOT HEAD and it describes the clue's H, the first letter of HOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A hothead is someone quick-tempered who acts rashly.

clue.text: One producing brandy to make girl calmer

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
stiller means more calm

explanation.surface: A spirit maker offering a drink to settle a young woman's nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: A distiller makes spirits such as brandy by distilling wine.

clue.text: Might it bite you in summer?

definitions.meaning: a venomous snake whose bite is a hazard
read as one who sums, a summer is one who adds

explanation.surface: A walker wonders whether something could bite them in the warm season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' looks like the season but is someone who does sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Adders are Britain's only venomous snake, and a person who adds figures is an adder.

clue.text: A prosthetic one cannot see at all

definitions.text: A prosthetic one cannot see at all

parts.words: A prosthetic one cannot see at all
parts.note: one refers to an organ of sight; an artificial replacement for it gives no vision

explanation.surface: An artificial version of something is wholly unable to see.
explanation.definitionFit: A false eye made of glass replaces a lost one cosmetically but gives no vision.

clue.text: Solicitor in bed, drinking whiskey

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a layer is a bed, as in a bed of rock
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A legal professional boozing while still between the sheets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinking' puts W inside LAYER.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a solicitor is a kind of lawyer who advises clients and prepares cases.
